title: Introduce probabilistic burst contract and smoothed utilization reporter for Dedicated fleets
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need a way to allow short-term bursts without violating long-term throughput guarantees. Current burst token pools are too binary (grant/reject) and produce utilization spikes that complicate autoscaler decisions. This change introduces a probabilistic burst contract (PBC) that smooths admission, plus a smoothed utilization reporter that feeds the autoscaler and telemetry with stable percentile-based signals.

What this PR does (single-line sections kept contiguous): Implements a leaky-bucket style contract where 'burst credit' is accrued and decayed with a tunable half-life; admissions are probabilistic when credit is depleted (admission probability = min(1, credit_ratio * scale + base_prob)) to allow graceful degradation under contention. Adds a new reporter that samples per-tenant request latencies and compute-utilization and publishes both raw percentiles (p50/p90/p99) and an EWMA-smoothed utilization metric used by the fleet autoscaler to avoid oscillation. Exposes config knobs in Dedicated API: burst_size, decay_half_life_seconds, base_admit_prob, admit_scale, reporter_window_seconds, reporter_sample_rate. Adds feature flag `pbc_enabled` for gradual rollout.

Design notes: The PBC keeps a token balance per-tenant; tokens refill at a steady rate proportional to the tenant's committed throughput and decay exponentially (configurable half-life) to prevent long-term hoarding. When tokens are insufficient we no longer block deterministically; instead we compute an admission probability that preserves long-term expected throughput while enabling intermittent bursts. The probabilistic approach reduces synchronized reject storms and smooths queueing. The reporter uses reservoir sampling for percentiles and an exponentially-weighted moving average for utilization (alpha derived from window_seconds).

Backward compatibility and safety: Behavior is opt-in via feature flag and per-tenant config. The deterministic admission path remains available (`pbc_enabled=false`) and default values align with current burst semantics (burst_size=2x alloc, base_admit_prob=0.0 yields approximate current behavior). All new metrics are additive and do not change existing metric names.

Telemetry and dashboards: New metrics added: `dedicated.burst.admitted_ratio`, `dedicated.burst.token_balance_ewma`, `dedicated.util.p50_ms`, `dedicated.util.p95_ms`, `dedicated.util.p99_ms`, `dedicated.util.smooth_ewma`. Dashboard JSON and Grafana snapshots included.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for admission math and decay; integration test harness simulating 1000 tenants with mixed load; canary rollout plan: enable PBC for 1% of tenants for 24h, monitor admitted_ratio and tail latencies, ramp to 25% then 100% if no regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Core algorithm implementation and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests against autoscaler simulation
- [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboard assets
- [x] API surface and config validation
- [x] Docs and feature-flag gating

References: Linear ENG-2201 (autoscale stability), ENG-2310 (dedicated burst design). Related incident SUP-412 inspired the probabilistic approach to avoid large reject waves.

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on parameter defaults and the interaction between reporter smoothing and the autoscaler's hysteresis. Performance-sensitive code is in `pkg/fleet/pbc` and `pkg/fleet/reporter` — those files contain hot paths where allocation/GC was carefully minimized.

release_notes: Adds a probabilistic burst admission mechanism and a smoothed utilization reporter for Dedicated fleets. New config knobs: burst_size, decay_half_life_seconds, base_admit_prob, admit_scale, reporter_window_seconds. Opt-in via feature flag. Improves autoscaler stability under bursty workloads and reduces reject wave incidents. Includes dashboards and alerts for monitoring admitted_ratio and smoothed utilization.
